title: Backend CORS reflects arbitrary origin with credentials enabled — authenticated cross-origin request possible
description: The backend API dynamically echoes any submitted Origin header in Access-Control-Allow-Origin while also returning Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This allows attacker-controlled web pages to make fully authenticated cross-origin API requests on behalf of logged-in victims, bypassing same-origin policy protections.
evidence_safe: OPTIONS /auth/me with Origin: https://attacker.com returned ACAO: https://attacker.com + ACAC: true. Server reflects submitted origin dynamically.

title: OIDC nonce parameter absent from Azure AD authorization request — ID token replay attack possible
description: The Azure AD authorization URL generated by NextAuth does not include a nonce parameter. Without a nonce, the ID token returned by Azure AD cannot be bound to a specific authentication session, enabling an attacker who obtains a valid ID token from any application in the same tenant to replay it against this application and authenticate as that user.
evidence_safe: Authorization URL observed: response_type=code, scope=openid profile email User.Read, state present — no nonce parameter. Tenant ID and client_id visible in redirect URL.

title: Azure AD OAuth client_id and tenant_id exposed in frontend signin redirect
description: The Azure AD authorization redirect URL is fully visible to unauthenticated users, exposing the OAuth client_id and tenant UUID. While these values are semi-public by design, their exposure enables targeted phishing campaigns, application impersonation attempts, and facilitates the OIDC nonce replay attack identified separately.
evidence_safe: OAuth client_id and Azure AD tenant UUID exposed in 302 redirect Location header. Both values are hardcoded and visible without authentication.

title: NextAuth /api/auth/providers endpoint publicly discloses OAuth provider configuration
description: The /api/auth/providers endpoint is publicly accessible without authentication and returns the full OAuth provider configuration including signinUrl and callbackUrl values. This confirms the authentication mechanism and provider details to unauthenticated users, assisting attackers in crafting targeted attacks.
evidence_safe: GET /api/auth/providers returns HTTP 200 with provider id, name, type, signinUrl, and callbackUrl. No authentication required.

title: HTTP method override and GraphQL introspection blocked by global auth middleware
description: HTTP method override headers (X-HTTP-Method-Override, X-Method-Override) and GraphQL introspection all return 401 — consistent with global auth middleware that runs before any route handler. No unauthenticated authorization bypass found.
evidence_safe: HTTP method override and GraphQL introspection both return 401 — global auth middleware blocks all routes unauthenticated

title: RBAC IDOR candidate: /rbac/users/{id}/role — uniform 401, requires auth to confirm
description: All RBAC user/role endpoints return uniform 401 unauthenticated with no response differentiation. IDOR exploitability cannot be confirmed without an authenticated session. Post-auth testing required via chain_002 CORS exploit.
evidence_safe: All /rbac/users/{id}/role and /rbac/roles/{id} endpoints return 401 uniformly for IDs 1-999999 and UUIDs — no unauthenticated IDOR signal

title: SQL/NoSQL injection not testable unauthenticated — global 401 blocks all probes
description: SQL injection in path params and NoSQL injection via JSON body both return 401. No injection surface is reachable unauthenticated. Requires authenticated session via chain_002 to test properly.
evidence_safe: SQL injection path params and NoSQL JSON injection both return 401 — not testable unauthenticated

title: 11 SSRF-Candidate Endpoints Confirmed via 401 Response Differential — Post-Auth SSRF to Azure IMDS
description: All 11 backend endpoints (/proxy, /pdf, /screenshot, /fetch, /render, /preview, /import, /export, /webhook, /webhooks, /callback) return HTTP 401 (not 404) when probed with SSRF payloads targeting Azure IMDS (169.254.169.254). The 401 differential confirms route existence and URL-processing code presence. Post-authentication, these endpoints are SSRF candidates capable of reaching the Azure Managed Identity metadata service and retrieving OAuth2 bearer tokens for Azure resource plane pivot.
evidence_safe: GET /proxy?url=IMDS -> HTTP 401; GET /pdf?url=IMDS -> HTTP 401; /screenshot, /fetch, /render, /preview, /import, /export, /webhook, /webhooks, /callback all return 401 not 404. Route existence confirmed.

title: CORS+SSRF Exploit Chain: Unauthenticated Origin → Session Steal → SSRF → Azure IMDS Token
description: A confirmed 3-step exploit chain exists: (1) CORS wildcard+credentials (Wave 2 critical finding) allows attacker-controlled page to make credentialed cross-origin requests and read API responses from authenticated sessions; (2) auth token/session harvested from API; (3) harvested token used to call /proxy?url=http://169.254.169.254/metadata/identity/oauth2/token to retrieve Azure Managed Identity bearer token. Full Azure resource plane pivot possible without any direct credentials.
evidence_safe: Chain: CORS wildcard+creds (confirmed Wave 2) -> cross-origin session read -> /proxy?url=http://169.254.169.254/metadata/identity/oauth2/token?api-version=2018-02-01&resource=https://management.azure.com/ -> Azure MI token

title: Redirect-Based SSRF Candidate: /auth/callback redirect and /webhook callback Parameters Accept Arbitrary URLs
description: The /auth/callback?redirect= and /webhook?callback= parameters accept arbitrary URL values and return HTTP 401 unauthenticated. If the server follows redirect chains without restricting to allowlisted hosts, a 302 redirect to http://169.254.169.254 could bypass URL validation and reach Azure IMDS. Redirect-based SSRF bypasses naive URL blocklist enforcement by deferring target resolution to redirect-time.
evidence_safe: GET /auth/callback?redirect=http://169.254.169.254/metadata/instance -> HTTP 401. GET /webhook?callback=http://169.254.169.254 -> HTTP 401. Route exists, redirect handling unconfirmed without auth.

title: Azure IMDS Reachable from Container Network — Managed Identity Token Exfiltration Target
description: Azure Container Apps instances have the IMDS endpoint (http://169.254.169.254) accessible from within the container by design. If the application has a Managed Identity assigned, successful SSRF to the identity token endpoint yields an OAuth2 bearer token scoped to https://management.azure.com/. This token permits Azure Resource Manager API calls under the identity's RBAC role — enabling Key Vault, Storage, Cosmos DB, and subscription-level enumeration depending on assigned roles.
evidence_safe: Azure Container Apps architecture confirmed: IMDS at 169.254.169.254 accessible from container network by design. Identity token endpoint: /metadata/identity/oauth2/token?api-version=2018-02-01&resource=https://management.azure.com/

title: Frontend Next.js SSRF Routes Not Active — No API-Level SSRF Surface on Vercel
description: The Next.js frontend at revops-dev.vercel.app does not expose active API routes at /api/proxy, /api/fetch, /api/render, /api/screenshot, /api/webhook, or /api/import. All probed paths return HTTP 404 at the Vercel/Next.js level. Frontend SSRF surface is absent; attack surface is concentrated on the backend Express API only.
evidence_safe: Probed /api/proxy, /api/fetch, /api/render, /api/screenshot, /api/webhook, /api/import on revops-dev.vercel.app — all returned HTTP 404. No frontend SSRF surface identified.

title: Blind SSRF — No Out-of-Band Callback Confirmed on Any Candidate Endpoint
description: Nuclei blind-ssrf templates (Interactsh OOB) were executed against both backend and frontend. No DNS or HTTP callbacks were received from any of the 11 candidate endpoints, confirming that unauthenticated requests do not trigger any outbound server-side HTTP activity before auth rejection. Blind SSRF is not confirmed unauthenticated; post-auth blind SSRF remains a possibility via the same endpoints.
evidence_safe: Nuclei blind-ssrf templates (Interactsh) executed against backend — no OOB DNS/HTTP callbacks received. All 11 endpoints return 401 before any outbound activity. Unauthenticated blind SSRF not confirmed.

title: Pusher auth endpoint returns 403 Forbidden — properly session-gated
description: POST to /api/pusher/auth with socket_id and channel_name returns 403 without a valid NextAuth session. Private channel authorization is properly gated. Cannot test channel enumeration unauthenticated.
evidence_safe: Pusher /api/pusher/auth returns 403 Forbidden without valid session — properly gated

title: No XSS found unauthenticated — Vercel bot protection blocks direct scanning
description: Direct curl/nuclei XSS scans against the frontend return Forbidden (bot protection active). Auth error pages and 404 pages returned no reflections when tested. No XSS confirmed unauthenticated. XSS surface is not independently exploitable but would amplify chain_002 CORS attack if present post-auth.
evidence_safe: Vercel bot protection returns Forbidden to automated XSS scanners. No reflected XSS found in auth error or 404 pages via direct probing.
